themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints spiked to 44 THIS WEEK, up 196% from the 8-week baseline average of 14.9 complaints per week (z-score: 4.09), suggesting a sudden deterioration in street-level noise quality that warrants immediate investigation into source and duration.
evidence: 44 vehicle noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 14.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (196% spike)
Z-score of 4.09 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Noise complaints represent 3rd-largest complaint category overall (1,096 street/sidewalk + vehicle combined over 90 days)
reporting_angles: What specific streets or corridors are generating complaints? Are there construction projects, street racing, or commercial delivery patterns driving the spike?
Interview residents and NYPD to understand if this is a temporary event or emerging pattern requiring enforcement response

themes_detail.label: Water Infrastructure Stress
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints jumped to 28 TWO WEEKS AGO, representing a 225% increase over the 8-week baseline of 8.6 complaints per week (z-score: 4.04), potentially signaling broader water main or pressure issues across the district.
evidence: 28 water system complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 8.6 weekly average (225% spike, z-score: 4.04)
Converges with persistent community board budget request for DEP sanitary sewer inspection and repair on specific street segments
Plumbing complaints also elevated at 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2 baseline (1100% spike, z-score: 4.16)
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to identify which water main segments are failing or under pressure; request maintenance records and projected repair timelines
Verify if water quality issues are accompanying quantity/pressure complaints; check for boil-water advisories or contamination reports

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Damaged street signs complaints reached 4 THIS WEEK, up 256% from the 8-week baseline of 1.1 per week (z-score: 3.68), indicating accelerating street-level infrastructure decay that may correlate with broader street condition complaints (594 over 90 days).
evidence: 4 damaged street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (256% spike, z-score: 3.68)
Street condition complaints remain consistently high at 594 over 90 days (ongoing baseline issue)
Suggests potential acceleration in infrastructure maintenance backlog
reporting_angles: Document specific damaged signs across the district via street-level reporting; assess whether damage is accidental, age-related, or impact-related
Request DOT maintenance data for CD 204 to determine backlog depth and repair timelines

themes_detail.label: Litter Basket Shortage
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests spiked to 3 complaints THREE WEEKS AGO, up 700% from the 8-week baseline of 0.4 per week (z-score: 5.42), suggesting residents are reporting inadequate street-level sanitation infrastructure despite a concurrent 39% drop in unsanitary condition complaints this week.
evidence: 3 litter basket requests 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Paradoxically occurs alongside 39% DROP in unsanitary condition complaints THIS WEEK (86 vs. 142.0 baseline), suggesting possible complaints reclassification or recent cleanup effort
Reflects persistent community concern with street cleanliness (dirty condition: 755 complaints over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Identify which blocks submitted litter basket requests; verify if new baskets were installed and whether that correlates with reduced unsanitary complaints
Interview Sanitation or Parks Dept. on basket placement strategy and resident feedback loop
